 Appearance:

2. sentences.text:
By way of the present petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "the Code"), petitioner has prayed for quashing and setting aside F.I.R.
bearing C.R.No.I-121 of 2014 registered with Sabarmati Police Station, Dist. Ahmedabad, which has been filed by respondent No.2- original complainant.
The said complaint has been filed for the offence punishable under Sections 363 and 366 of the Indian Penal Code.

Subsequently, after the police report, an additional offence punishable under Sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code,
Sections 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 3(1) (12) &
3(2)(5) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 was added, and to quash all other consequential proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR qua the applicant.
5. Learned advocate for the petitioner has taken this Court through the factual matrix arising out of the present petition.

sentences.text: At the outset, it is submitted that the parties have amicably resolved the issue and therefore, any NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3715/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined further continuance of the proceedings pursuant to the impugned FIR as well as any further proceedings arising therefrom would create hardship to the petitioner.

It is submitted that respondent No.2 mother of the victim has filed an affidavit dated 10.12.2024 in these proceedings and has declared that the dispute between the petitioner and respondent No.2 is resolved.
It is further submitted that victim has been married and a child born out of wedlock and is living happily.
In view of the fact that the dispute is resolved, the trial would be futile and any further continuance of the proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law.
It is therefore submitted that this Court may exercise its inherent powers conferred under Section 482 of the Code and allow the application as prayed for.

6. Learned advocate Ms.Abha Makwana for respondent No.2-original complainant has placed on record an Affidavit dated 10.12.2024 duly sworn by the original complainant-Ms.Parulben Shankarbhai Chauhan and submitted that the original complainant does not wish to proceed further with the matter.

She further submitted that the victim has got married, and with the said wedlock,
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/3715/2015 ORDER DATED: 10/12/2024 undefined she has a child.
She has placed on record the birth certificate which is taken on record.
6.1 The original complainant - Mrs. Parulben Shankarbhai Chauhan is present in person before the Court and is identified by learned advocate for respondent No.2.

Upon inquiry made by the Court,
she has declared before this Court that she does not wish to proceed further with the matter and has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the present petition and submitted that considering the seriousness of the offence, the complaint in question may not be quashed and the present petition may be rejected.
8. Heard learned advocates for the parties and considered the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case as well as affidavit of original complainant dated 10.12.2024.

The original complainant,
being a mother of the victim, has also expressed her willingness not to pursue with the impugned FIR as victim has already married and settled in her life with a child borne out of NEUTRAL

Ahmedabad, filed against present petitioner, is hereby quashed and set aside and all other consequential proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR, are also quashed and set aside qua the petitioner.
Accordingly, Rule is made absolute.

9.1 Moreover, if any, amount has been received by the original complainant in view of the complaint filed by complainant, by virtue of filing the said complaint, the same shall be returned back to the Government within a period of two months.
